name: White oak boards
appearance: Warm honey grain with visible knots; reads natural and slightly rustic.
maintenance: Sweep often, damp-mop rarely, re-oil or re-lacquer every few years.
durability: Hard enough for family living if finished well; dents from grit and heels.
bestFor: Living rooms, bedrooms, and open-plan social spaces.

name: Luxury vinyl plank
appearance: Printed wood or stone look with a wear layer; very even colour.
maintenance: Mop with a pH-neutral cleaner. Avoid steam and standing water at joints.
durability: Excellent for kitchens and rentals; quality depends on wear-layer thickness.
bestFor: Kitchens, apartments, and high-traffic halls.

name: Porcelain tile
appearance: Crisp, often stone- or concrete-look, with grout lines as part of the pattern.
maintenance: Easy to wash; grout needs sealing or a darker grout to hide staining.
durability: Very hard and water-resistant; cold underfoot unless heated.
bestFor: Bathrooms, kitchens, entries, and hot climates.

name: Terrazzo
appearance: Speckled chips in a cement or resin field — graphic and enduring.
maintenance: Seal periodically; wipe spills. Avoid harsh acids on cement terrazzo.
durability: Extremely long-lived when installed well; a statement surface.
bestFor: Entries, kitchens, and bathrooms that can carry a bold floor.

name: Wool-blend carpet
appearance: Soft, matte pile that warms a room and quiets sound.
maintenance: Vacuum regularly; professional clean as needed. Spills need prompt blotting.
durability: Comfortable but wears in traffic paths; better in bedrooms than kitchens.
bestFor: Bedrooms and quiet sitting rooms.

name: Polished concrete
appearance: Mineral grey with aggregate flecks; industrial and continuous.
maintenance: Seal and dust-mop. Rugs help with acoustics and warmth.
durability: Very durable; can crack if the slab moves. Cold without underfloor heat.
bestFor: Industrial and modern interiors, garages converted to living.

name: Strand-woven bamboo
appearance: Fine linear grain, usually honey or carbonised brown.
maintenance: Similar to hardwood: dry clean, avoid excess water.
durability: Strand-woven is harder than many oaks; still dislikes wet rooms.
bestFor: Living areas when you want a renewable wood look.

name: Honed limestone
appearance: Soft, cloudy stone in cream or taupe with subtle fossils.
maintenance: Seal well; wipe acids immediately. Use stone-safe cleaners.
durability: Softer than porcelain; beautiful in lower-traffic, well-sealed rooms.
bestFor: Bathrooms and calm living rooms in traditional homes.

name: Warm clay emulsion
appearance: Muted terracotta-pink that shifts with daylight.
maintenance: Wipeable if using a kitchen-and-bath or durable emulsion.
durability: Standard wall paint; two coats over a sealed primer.
bestFor: Living rooms and dining nooks in traditional or modern schemes.

name: Linen white
appearance: Soft off-white with a hint of yellow, not a cold brilliant white.
maintenance: Shows scuffs; keep a touch-up tin. Washable formulations help halls.
durability: Good general wall colour; ceilings often a cleaner white.
bestFor: Whole-home bases, ceilings, and minimalist rooms.

name: Sage green
appearance: Grey-green that sits quietly behind timber and brass.
maintenance: Mid-tones hide marks better than white.
durability: Typical emulsion performance; use moisture-resistant paint in baths.
bestFor: Bedrooms, studies, and kitchen cabinets as a painted finish.

name: Ink navy
appearance: Deep blue-black that makes rooms feel tailored and smaller in a good way.
maintenance: Dark colours show dust on skirtings; washable eggshell on woodwork.
durability: Needs thorough priming; two to three coats for even colour.
bestFor: Studies, dining rooms, and one feature wall.

name: Putty beige
appearance: Greige with warmth; a modern substitute for builder beige.
maintenance: Forgiving of fingerprints compared with bright white.
durability: Reliable all-rounder for rental-friendly refreshes.
bestFor: Halls, open-plan living, and pairing with oak floors.

name: Mineral limewash look
appearance: Cloudy, chalky movement rather than a flat plastic film.
maintenance: Not as washable as vinyl emulsion; better in low-splash rooms.
durability: Breathable; beautiful on masonry. Follow the maker's sealing advice.
bestFor: Feature walls, traditional rooms, and dry living spaces.

name: Standing-seam metal
appearance: Long vertical ribs in charcoal, copper, or pale grey.
maintenance: Low; check fasteners and flashings. Colour-coated steel lasts decades.
durability: Excellent in rain; noisy in hail unless insulated.
bestFor: Modern and industrial houses; lightweight over timber frames.

name: Clay tiles
appearance: Terracotta or glazed profiles with deep shadow lines.
maintenance: Replace cracked tiles; keep gutters clear. Heavy — structure must suit.
durability: Very long life in the right climate; vulnerable to freeze-thaw if poorly fired.
bestFor: Traditional and Mediterranean-inspired homes.

name: Asphalt shingles
appearance: Granular, layered tabs in grey, brown, or charcoal.
maintenance: Inspect after storms; lifespan shorter than clay or metal.
durability: Economical and common; wind ratings vary by product.
bestFor: Budget-conscious houses where local practice favours shingles.

name: Extensive green roof
appearance: A living carpet of sedum and moss over a waterproof build-up.
maintenance: Weeding, irrigation in drought, and drain checks. Not DIY structure.
durability: The membrane is the critical layer; planting is a wearing surface.
bestFor: Flat or low-pitch roofs with engineered loading and drainage.

name: Engineered quartz
appearance: Consistent speckles or veining; polished or honed.
maintenance: Soap and water. No sealing. Avoid high heat and strong solvents.
durability: Hard and non-porous; popular in family kitchens.
bestFor: Kitchens and bathrooms that need low-maintenance worktops.

name: Natural granite
appearance: Unique mineral pattern; each slab is different.
maintenance: Seal periodically. Wipe acids. Hot pans are usually fine.
durability: Very hard; can chip at edges. Heavy — cabinets must be sound.
bestFor: Traditional kitchens and statement islands.

name: Butcher-block timber
appearance: End- or edge-grain wood, oiled to a warm sheen.
maintenance: Oil regularly; never leave standing water. Can be sanded back.
durability: Living surface that scars; not ideal beside a sink unless well-oiled.
bestFor: Islands, baker's benches, and mixed-material kitchens.

name: High-pressure laminate
appearance: Printed stone or timber look with a thin build.
maintenance: Easy wipe-down. Avoid cutting directly on the surface and excess heat.
durability: Good value; joints and edges are the weak points.
bestFor: Budget kitchens, laundries, and rental refreshes.

name: Honied marble
appearance: Soft veining on a pale ground; luxurious and light-reflective.
maintenance: Sealing plus immediate wipe of wine, citrus, and oil. Etches from acid.
durability: Softer stone; patina is part of the look, not a flaw to everyone.
bestFor: Pastry stations, bathrooms, and traditional interiors.

name: Cast concrete
appearance: Monolithic, slightly imperfect, industrial.
maintenance: Seal thoroughly; hairline cracks can appear and are often accepted.
durability: Hard and heavy; custom formwork. Heat-tolerant if sealed.
bestFor: Industrial and modern kitchens, outdoor bars with proper mix.
